text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Audit a data collection pipeline configuration (fluentd-style) and report
# its key settings as a comma separated list.

set -uo pipefail

# Count top-level occurrences of a directive block such as <source>, <match **>.
count_directives() {
    local file=$1 name=$2
    local hits
    hits=$(grep -E -c "^[[:space:]]*<${name}([[:space:]>]|$)" "$file")
    echo $((hits))
}

# Fetch the first value of a parameter, ignoring trailing comments.
get_param() {
    local file=$1 key=$2 default=$3
    local raw
    raw=$(grep -E -m1 "^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]+" "$file")
    if [[ -z $raw ]]; then
        echo "$default"
        return
    fi
    local stripped
    stripped=$(cut -d'#' -f1 <<<"$raw")
    local value
    value=$(awk '{print $2}' <<<"$stripped")
    echo "${value:-$default}"
}

audit() {
    local pipeline=$1
    local sources matches filters bind port log_level flush chunk

    sources=$(count_directives "$pipeline" source)
    matches=$(count_directives "$pipeline" match)
    filters=$(count_directives "$pipeline" filter)

    bind=$(get_param "$pipeline" bind 0.0.0.0)
    port=$(get_param "$pipeline" port 24224)
    log_level=$(get_param "$pipeline" log_level info)
    flush=$(get_param "$pipeline" flush_interval 60s)
    chunk=$(get_param "$pipeline" chunk_limit_size 8M)

    printf '%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s\n' \
        "$sources" "$matches" "$filters" "$bind" \
        "$port" "$log_level" "$flush" "$chunk"
}

main() {
    if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "usage: $(basename "$0") <pipeline.conf>" >&2
        exit 2
    fi

    local pipeline=$1
    if [[ ! -r $pipeline ]]; then
        echo "audit: cannot read '$pipeline'" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    audit "$pipeline"
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extract build metadata from a Gradle-style automation build script.

set -u

unquote() {
    local value=$1
    value=${value%%//*}
    value=${value//\'/}
    value=${value//\"/}
    value=${value#JavaVersion.VERSION_}
    value=${value//_/.}
    # strip surrounding whitespace
    read -r value <<<"$value"
    printf '%s\n' "$value"
}

extract_plugin() {
    local script=$1 plugin
    plugin=$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*id[[:space:]]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"].*/\1/p" "$script" | head -n 1)
    if [ -z "$plugin" ]; then
        plugin=$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*apply[[:space:]]*plugin:[[:space:]]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"].*/\1/p" "$script" | head -n 1)
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${plugin:-none}"
}

extract_property() {
    local script=$1 key=$2 raw
    raw=$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p" "$script" | head -n 1)
    if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
        raw=$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]*\.set(\(.*\))[[:space:]]*$/\1/p" "$script" | head -n 1)
    fi
    if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "unknown"
    else
        unquote "$raw"
    fi
}

count_dependencies() {
    local script=$1 pattern=$2
    grep -cE "^[[:space:]]*${pattern}[[:space:](]" "$script"
}

extract_main_class() {
    local script=$1 raw
    raw=$(extract_property "$script" "mainClassName")
    if [ "$raw" = "unknown" ]; then
        raw=$(extract_property "$script" "mainClass")
    fi
    if [ "$raw" = "unknown" ]; then
        raw=$(sed -n "s/.*['\"]Main-Class['\"][[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\(.*\)/\1/p" "$script" | head -n 1)
        raw=$(unquote "${raw%,}")
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${raw:-unknown}"
}

evaluate() {
    local script=$1
    if [ ! -f "$script" ]; then
        printf '%s: no such build script\n' "$script" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local plugin target source group version compile test main
    plugin=$(extract_plugin "$script")
    target=$(extract_property "$script" "targetCompatibility")
    source=$(extract_property "$script" "sourceCompatibility")
    group=$(extract_property "$script" "group")
    version=$(extract_property "$script" "version")
    compile=$(count_dependencies "$script" "(implementation|api|compile|compileOnly)")
    test=$(count_dependencies "$script" "(testImplementation|testCompile|testRuntimeOnly)")
    main=$(extract_main_class "$script")
    printf '%s %s %s %s %s %s %s %s\n' \
        "$plugin" "$target" "$source" "$group" "$version" "$compile" "$test" "$main"
}

evaluate "$@"

`benchmark(directory)`
Finds all text files within the provided directory path. For each file, calculates its original size in bytes. Compresses the file using the standard gzip tool. Calculates the new compressed size in bytes. Computes the compression ratio using a basic calculator tool. Retrieves the exact modification time of the new archive. Prints a summary report including the file count and total space saved.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# benchmark(directory): gzip compression benchmark over the text files of a directory.

set -u

file_size() {
    local path=$1
    wc -c < "$path" | tr -d ' '
}

is_text_file() {
    local path=$1
    local kind
    kind=$(file --brief --mime-type "$path")
    [[ $kind == text/* ]]
}

compress_file() {
    local src=$1
    local archive="$src.gz"
    gzip --best --force --stdout "$src" > "$archive" || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$archive"
}

compression_ratio() {
    local original=$1 compressed=$2
    printf 'scale=3; %s / %s\n' "$compressed" "$original" | bc
}

archive_mtime() {
    local archive=$1
    date -r "$archive" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'
}

benchmark() {
    local directory=$1
    if [[ ! -d $directory ]]; then
        echo "benchmark: no such directory: $directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local count=0 saved=0
    local path archive original compressed ratio stamp

    while IFS= read -r path; do
        is_text_file "$path" || continue

        original=$(file_size "$path")
        archive=$(compress_file "$path") || continue
        compressed=$(file_size "$archive")
        ratio=$(compression_ratio "$original" "$compressed")
        stamp=$(archive_mtime "$archive")

        printf '%-40s %8s B -> %8s B  ratio %s  archived %s\n' \
            "$path" "$original" "$compressed" "$ratio" "$stamp"

        count=$((count + 1))
        saved=$((saved + original - compressed))
    done < <(find "$directory" -type f ! -name '*.gz')

    echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
    echo "text files compressed : $count"
    echo "total space saved     : $saved bytes"
    if (( count > 0 )); then
        echo "average saving/file   : $(printf 'scale=1; %s / %s\n' "$saved" "$count" | bc) bytes"
    fi
}

main() {
    local target=${1:-$(pwd)}
    benchmark "$target"
}

main "$@"

`aggregate(logfile)`
Extracts the date string from the very first line of the given log document. Counts the total number of lines in the document. Extracts all lines that contain the word error in any case. Counts how many unique error messages exist. Identifies the single most frequent error message. Extracts the timestamp of the very last error occurrence. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# aggregate: summarise a log file (date, size, errors).
set -uo pipefail

log_date() {
    local first
    first=$(head -n 1 "$1")
    local stamp
    stamp=$(printf '%s\n' "$first" | grep -oE '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}')
    if [ -n "$stamp" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$stamp"
    else
        printf 'unknown date\n'
    fi
}

line_count() {
    awk 'END { print NR }' "$1"
}

error_lines() {
    grep -i 'error' "$1"
}

strip_stamp() {
    sed -E 's/^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}([T ][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})?[[:space:]]*//'
}

unique_errors() {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | strip_stamp | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

top_error() {
    local ranked
    ranked=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | strip_stamp | sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr | head -n 1)

`convert(directory)`
Locates all plain text documents in the specified directory. For each document, determines its mime encoding using the standard file identification tool. If the encoding is not standard unicode, converts the content using the iconv tool and saves it to a temporary location. Measures the byte sizes of both the original and converted documents. Computes the size difference. Replaces the original document if the process succeeds. Counts the total processed documents.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Recode non-unicode plain text documents in a directory tree to UTF-8.

set -u

mime_type() {
    file -b --mime-type -- "$1"
}

mime_encoding() {
    file -b --mime-encoding -- "$1"
}

file_size() {
    wc -c < "$1" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

is_standard_unicode() {
    case "$1" in
        utf-8|utf-16le|utf-16be|us-ascii) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# Recode a document into a temporary file and print that file's path.
recode_to_temp() {
    local document=$1 encoding=$2 temp
    temp=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/convert.XXXXXX") || return 1
    if iconv -f "$encoding" -t UTF-8 -o "$temp" -- "$document" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '%s\n' "$temp"
    else
        rm -f "$temp"
        return 1
    fi
}

report() {
    printf '%-50s %-12s %8s -> %8s (%+d bytes)\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5"
}

convert() {
    local directory=$1
    if [ ! -d "$directory" ]; then
        printf '%s: not a directory\n' "$directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local document encoding temp before after delta count=0
    while IFS= read -r document; do
        [ "$(mime_type "$document")" = "text/plain" ] || continue

        encoding=$(mime_encoding "$document")
        is_standard_unicode "$encoding" && continue

        if ! temp=$(recode_to_temp "$document" "$encoding"); then
            printf 'failed to recode %s from %s\n' "$document" "$encoding" >&2
            continue
        fi

        before=$(file_size "$document")
        after=$(file_size "$temp")
        delta=$((after - before))

        if mv -f -- "$temp" "$document"; then
            report "$document" "$encoding" "$before" "$after" "$delta"
            count=$((count + 1))
        else
            rm -f "$temp"
        fi
    done < <(find "$directory" -type f)

    printf 'converted %d document(s) under %s\n' "$count" "$directory"
}

convert "${1:-$(pwd)}"

text_es:
`lint(directory)`
Finds all files ending in sh within the folder. For each script, validates its syntax using the bash tool with the check flag. Captures any error output produced. Extracts the first error message line if one exists. Determines the system owner of the script. Counts the total lines of code in the script. Accumulates the total number of scripts analyzed and the count of those containing errors.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lint(directory): syntax-check every *.sh script under a directory and report.

lint() {
    local directory="$1"
    local script errors first_error owner lines
    local total=0 bad=0

    if [[ ! -d "$directory" ]]; then
        echo "lint: not a directory: $directory" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    printf '%-40s %-10s %6s %s\n' "SCRIPT" "OWNER" "LINES" "STATUS"

    while IFS= read -r script; do
        total=$((total + 1))
        errors=$(bash -n "$script" 2>&1)
        owner=$(script_owner "$script")
        lines=$(count_lines "$script")

        if [[ -n "$errors" ]]; then
            bad=$((bad + 1))
            first_error=$(head -n 1 <<<"$errors")
            printf '%-40s %-10s %6s %s\n' "$script" "$owner" "$lines" "$first_error"
        else
            printf '%-40s %-10s %6s %s\n' "$script" "$owner" "$lines" "OK"
        fi
    done < <(find_scripts "$directory")

    echo "---"
    echo "scripts analyzed: $total"
    echo "scripts with errors: $bad"

    [[ $bad -eq 0 ]]
}

find_scripts() {
    find "$1" -type f -name '*.sh' -print | sort
}

script_owner() {
    local owner
    owner=$(stat -c '%U' "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ -z "$owner" ]]; then
        owner=$(stat -f '%Su' "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    fi
    echo "${owner:-unknown}"
}

count_lines() {
    local counted
    counted=$(wc -l <"$1")
    echo "$((counted))"
}

main() {
    local target="${1:-.}"
    local resolved

    resolved=$(cd -- "$target" 2>/dev/null && pwd) || {
        echo "main: cannot access $target" >&2
        exit 2
    }

    echo "Linting shell scripts under $resolved"
    lint "$resolved"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
`validate(filepath)`
Reads a plain text file containing one password per line. For each entry, calculates its character length. Counts the number of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numeric digits, and special symbols using standard text filters. Checks if the entry appears in a local weak passwords dictionary file. Calculates an overall numeric score based on these counts. Aggregates the highest score found across all entries.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Password strength auditor.

WEAK_DICT="${WEAK_DICT:-./weak-passwords.txt}"

count_class() {
    local pw="$1" class="$2"
    local hits
    hits=$(printf '%s' "$pw" | grep -o "[$class]" | wc -l)
    echo "$hits"
}

is_weak() {
    local pw="$1"
    [ -f "$WEAK_DICT" ] || return 1
    grep -qxF -- "$pw" "$WEAK_DICT"
}

score_entry() {
    local pw="$1"
    local len=${#pw}
    local upper lower digits symbols score
    upper=$(count_class "$pw" 'A-Z')
    lower=$(count_class "$pw" 'a-z')
    digits=$(count_class "$pw" '0-9')
    symbols=$((len - upper - lower - digits))

    score=$((len * 2))
    [ "$upper" -gt 0 ] && score=$((score + 10))
    [ "$lower" -gt 0 ] && score=$((score + 10))
    [ "$digits" -gt 0 ] && score=$((score + 15))
    [ "$symbols" -gt 0 ] && score=$((score + 20))
    if is_weak "$pw"; then
        score=$((score - 50))
    fi
    [ "$score" -lt 0 ] && score=0

    printf '%d %d %d %d %d %d\n' "$len" "$upper" "$lower" "$digits" "$symbols" "$score"
}

validate() {
    local filepath="$1"
    if [ ! -r "$filepath" ]; then
        echo "validate: cannot read '$filepath'" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local best=0 line stats verdict
    printf '%-24s %4s %3s %3s %3s %3s %6s %s\n' \
        PASSWORD LEN UP LOW DIG SYM SCORE VERDICT
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        [ -n "$line" ] || continue
        stats=$(score_entry "$line")
        set -- $stats
        verdict="ok"
        is_weak "$line" && verdict="weak-dictionary"
        printf '%-24s %4s %3s %3s %3s %3s %6s %s\n' \
            "$line" "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$6" "$verdict"
        [ "$6" -gt "$best" ] && best="$6"
    done < "$filepath"

    echo "entries scanned: $(grep -c '[^[:space:]]' "$filepath")"
    echo "highest score:   $best"
}

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "usage: $(basename "$0") PASSWORD_FILE" >&2
    exit 2
fi
validate "$1"

`analyze(document)`
Processes a raw text document by first converting all characters to lowercase. Counts the total number of words. Counts how many words match entries in a local positive word list and a negative word list. Calculates a final sentiment score by subtracting negative matches from positive ones and dividing by total words. Identifies the most frequently used word that is longer than five characters. Extracts the very first sentence for context.

`summarize(username)`
Queries the system password database to extract the full real name of the specified user. Locates their designated home directory path. Counts the number of hidden configuration files present in that directory. Retrieves the timestamp of their most recent system login. Counts how many processes they are currently running. Sums up the total resident memory used by all their active processes. Identifies their default login shell.

`standardize(directory)`
Finds all jpeg images in the specified folder. Retrieves the current pixel width and height of each image using the identify tool. For images wider than a maximum threshold, calculates a proportionally scaled height. Resizes the image using the standard image conversion utility. Measures the file size of the newly generated image. Extracts the base filename to append a resized suffix. Counts the total number of modified images.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# standardize: resize oversized JPEG images in a directory to a maximum width.

set -o pipefail

MAX_WIDTH=1024

image_width() {
    identify -format '%w' "$1"
}

image_height() {
    identify -format '%h' "$1"
}

scaled_height() {
    local width="$1" height="$2"
    echo $(( (height * MAX_WIDTH + width / 2) / width ))
}

resized_name() {
    local path="$1"
    local dir base
    dir=$(dirname "$path")
    base=$(basename "$path" .jpg)
    base=$(basename "$base" .jpeg)
    printf '%s/%s_resized.jpg\n' "$dir" "$base"
}

human_size() {
    local bytes
    bytes=$(stat -c '%s' "$1")
    awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN { if (b < 1048576) printf "%.1f KiB", b/1024; else printf "%.2f MiB", b/1048576 }'
}

standardize() {
    local directory="$1"
    if [ ! -d "$directory" ]; then
        echo "standardize: '$directory' is not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local count=0 image width height new_height target size
    while IFS= read -r image; do
        width=$(image_width "$image")
        if [ -z "$width" ] || [ "$width" -le "$MAX_WIDTH" ]; then
            continue
        fi
        height=$(image_height "$image")
        new_height=$(scaled_height "$width" "$height")
        target=$(resized_name "$image")

        if ! convert "$image" -resize "${MAX_WIDTH}x${new_height}" "$target"; then
            echo "standardize: failed to convert '$image'" >&2
            continue
        fi

        size=$(human_size "$target")
        printf '%s: %sx%s -> %sx%s (%s)\n' \
            "$image" "$width" "$height" "$MAX_WIDTH" "$new_height" "$size"
        count=$((count + 1))
    done < <(find "$directory" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
                  \( -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.jpeg' \) \
                  -not -iname '*_resized.jpg' | sort)

    echo "Modified $count image(s) in $directory"
}

main() {
    local dir="${1:-.}"
    standardize "$(realpath "$dir")"
}

main "$@"

`validate(config)`
Parses a standard initialization style configuration file. Extracts the value assigned to the network port setting. Verifies that the extracted port consists only of numeric digits. Checks active network connections to see if that port is already in use. Extracts the designated log directory path. Checks the octal permissions of that directory. Retrieves the username of the account that owns the configuration file.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validates an INI-style configuration file: network port and log directory.

set -u

get_setting() {
    local file=$1 key=$2 raw
    raw=$(sed -n -E "s/^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*(.*)$/\1/p" "$file" | tail -n 1)
    raw=${raw%%[;#]*}
    printf '%s\n' "$(sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//' <<<"$raw")"
}

port_in_use() {
    local port=$1 listeners
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        listeners=$(ss -Hltn 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}')
    else
        listeners=$(netstat -ltn 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>2 {print $4}')
    fi
    grep -qE "[:.]${port}\$" <<<"$listeners"
}

validate() {
    local config=$1

    if [ ! -f "$config" ]; then
        printf 'error: configuration file not found: %s\n' "$config" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local owner
    owner=$(stat -c '%U' "$config")
    printf 'config owner: %s\n' "$owner"

text_es:
`shift(subtitle)`
Reads an srt format subtitle file. Identifies all lines containing timing arrows. Extracts the very last timestamp in the file to determine total duration. Calculates a new shifted timestamp by adding a fixed millisecond delay. Replaces the original timestamps with the adjusted ones. Counts the total number of dialogue text blocks. Extracts the base filename to generate a new output file path.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-time an .srt subtitle file by a fixed delay.
set -uo pipefail

DELAY_MS=2000

# The name "shift" is a shell builtin; disable it so this script's own
# definition is the only meaning of the word here.
enable -n shift

ts_to_ms() {
    local ts=$1 h m s ms
    h=${ts:0:2}; m=${ts:3:2}; s=${ts:6:2}; ms=${ts:9:3}
    echo $(( 10#$h * 3600000 + 10#$m * 60000 + 10#$s * 1000 + 10#$ms ))
}

ms_to_ts() {
    local total=$1
    printf '%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d' \
        $(( total / 3600000 )) $(( total / 60000 % 60 )) \
        $(( total / 1000 % 60 )) $(( total % 1000 ))
}

shift_timestamp() {
    local ms
    ms=$(ts_to_ms "$1")
    ms_to_ts $(( ms + DELAY_MS ))
}

shift_arrow_line() {
    local start end first second
    read -r first _ second _ <<<"$1"
    start=$(shift_timestamp "$first")
    end=$(shift_timestamp "$second")
    printf '%s --> %s\n' "$start" "$end"
}

shift() {
    local subtitle=$1 dir base out last_line last_ts total blocks line

    dir=$(dirname "$subtitle")
    base=$(basename "$subtitle" .srt)
    out="$dir/${base}.shifted.srt"

    last_line=$(grep -- '-->' "$subtitle" | tail -n 1)
    if [[ -z $last_line ]]; then
        printf 'No timing arrows found in %s\n' "$subtitle" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    last_ts=${last_line##*--> }
    last_ts=${last_ts%$'\r'}
    total=$(ts_to_ms "$last_ts")

    : >"$out"
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
        line=${line%$'\r'}
        if [[ $line == *'-->'* ]]; then
            shift_arrow_line "$line" >>"$out"
        else
            printf '%s\n' "$line" >>"$out"
        fi
    done <"$subtitle"

    blocks=$(grep -c -- '-->' "$out")
    printf 'Original duration : %s\n' "$(ms_to_ts "$total")"
    printf 'Shifted duration  : %s\n' "$(ms_to_ts $(( total + DELAY_MS )))"
    printf 'Dialogue blocks   : %d\n' "$blocks"
    printf 'Output file       : %s\n' "$out"
}

main() {
    if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
        printf 'usage: %s <subtitle.srt>\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [[ ! -r $1 ]]; then
        printf '%s: cannot read file\n' "$1" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    shift "$1"
}

main "$@"

text_es:
`trim(document)`
Processes a text document to remove inefficient formatting. Strips trailing space characters from the end of every line. Condenses multiple consecutive blank lines down to a single blank line. Saves the result to a temporary scratch file. Counts the total lines and characters in the original file. Counts the total lines and characters in the new file. Calculates the exact number of bytes saved before replacing the original.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# trim - strip trailing blanks and collapse repeated empty lines in place
set -u

count_lines() {
    awk 'END { print NR }' "$1"
}

count_chars() {
    wc -c < "$1" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

squeeze() {
    sed -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "$1" | cat -s
}

format_size() {
    awk -v b="$1" 'BEGIN {
        if (b < 1024) printf "%d B\n", b
        else printf "%.1f KiB\n", b / 1024
    }'
}

report() {
    printf '  %-9s %6s lines %9s chars\n' "$1" "$2" "$3"
}

TRIM_SAVED=0

trim() {
    local document=$1
    if [ ! -f "$document" ] || [ ! -r "$document" ]; then
        printf 'trim: %s: not a readable regular file\n' "$document" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local orig_lines=$(count_lines "$document")
    local orig_chars=$(count_chars "$document")

    local scratch=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trim.XXXXXX")
    squeeze "$document" > "$scratch"

    local new_lines=$(count_lines "$scratch")
    local new_chars=$(count_chars "$scratch")
    local saved=$(( orig_chars - new_chars ))
    local dropped=$(( orig_lines - new_lines ))
    local pretty=$(format_size "$saved")

    printf '%s\n' "$document"
    report original "$orig_lines" "$orig_chars"
    report trimmed "$new_lines" "$new_chars"
    printf '  saved %s in %d fewer lines\n' "$pretty" "$dropped"

    local mode=$(stat -c '%a' "$document" 2>/dev/null || stat -f '%Lp' "$document")
    mv -f "$scratch" "$document"
    chmod "$mode" "$document"

    TRIM_SAVED=$saved
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s document [document ...]\n' "${0##*/}" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local total=0 status=0 doc
    for doc in "$@"; do
        if trim "$doc"; then
            total=$(( total + TRIM_SAVED ))
        else
            status=1
        fi
    done

    local human=$(format_size "$total")
    printf 'total reclaimed: %s\n' "$human"
    return "$status"
}

main "$@"

`generate(markdown)`
Reads a markdown formatted text file. Extracts all lines that begin with heading hash symbols. Counts the total number of headings found. Determines the structural depth of each heading by counting the hash characters. Strips the symbols to isolate the plain text title. Converts that title into a lowercase anchor link by replacing spaces with hyphens. Extracts the original filename to create a modified version with the new index prepended.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds a table-of-contents index from the headings of a markdown file
# and writes it to a new file whose name carries the "index_" prefix.

set -u

heading_depth() {
    local hashes
    hashes=$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's/^(#+).*/\1/')
    printf '%s' "${#hashes}"
}

heading_title() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's/^#+[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]+$//'
}

make_anchor() {
    local lowered
    lowered=$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    printf '%s' "$lowered" | sed -E 's/[^a-z0-9 -]//g; s/ /-/g'
}

index_filename() {
    local dir base
    dir=$(dirname "$1")
    base=$(basename "$1")
    if [ "$dir" = "." ]; then
        printf 'index_%s' "$base"
    else
        printf '%s/index_%s' "$dir" "$base"
    fi
}

generate() {
    local markdown=$1
    if [ ! -r "$markdown" ]; then
        printf 'generate: cannot read %s\n' "$markdown" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local headings
    headings=$(grep -E '^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]' "$markdown")
    if [ -z "$headings" ]; then
        printf 'generate: no headings in %s\n' "$markdown" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local total
    total=$(printf '%s\n' "$headings" | grep -c '')
    local target
    target=$(index_filename "$markdown")

    {
        printf '# Table of Contents (%d headings)\n\n' "$total"
        local line depth title anchor indent
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            depth=$(heading_depth "$line")
            title=$(heading_title "$line")
            anchor=$(make_anchor "$title")
            indent=$(printf '%*s' $(( (depth - 1) * 2 )) '')
            printf '%s- [%s](#%s)\n' "$indent" "$title" "$anchor"
        done <<< "$headings"
        printf '\n'
        cat "$markdown"
    } > "$target"

    printf 'Wrote %s with %d headings\n' "$target" "$total"
}

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
    prog=$(basename "$0")
    printf 'usage: %s <file.md>\n' "$prog" >&2
    exit 2
fi
generate "$1"

text_es:
`cleanup(archive)`
Scans an archive directory for compressed log files that are older than thirty days. Calculates the total disk space consumed by these specific files before taking action. Extracts the creation date embedded in the filename of the oldest identified log. Counts the exact number of files slated for removal. Deletes the old files. Retrieves the available free disk space on the partition after the deletion completes.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# cleanup(archive): purge compressed logs older than 30 days and report on the run.
set -u

find_old_files() {
    local archive=$1
    find "$archive" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
        \( -name '*.gz' -o -name '*.bz2' -o -name '*.xz' -o -name '*.zip' \) \
        -mtime +30 -print | sort
}

total_size() {
    local total=0 file size
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        size=$(stat -c %s -- "$file")
        total=$(( total + size ))
    done
    echo "$total"
}

human_size() {
    numfmt --to=iec --suffix=B --format='%.1f' "$1"
}

oldest_date() {
    local stamp
    stamp=$(sed -nE 's/.*[^0-9]([0-9]{8})([^0-9].*)?$/\1/p' | sort -n | head -n 1)
    if [ -n "$stamp" ]; then
        date -d "$stamp" +%Y-%m-%d
    else
        echo "unknown"
    fi
}

delete_files() {
    local file
    while IFS= read -r file; do
        rm -f -- "$file"
    done
}

free_space() {
    local kbytes
    kbytes=$(df -Pk "$1" | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }')
    human_size $(( kbytes * 1024 ))
}

cleanup() {
    local archive=$1 candidates count bytes oldest
    if [ ! -d "$archive" ]; then
        echo "cleanup: $archive: not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    candidates=$(find_old_files "$archive")
    if [ -z "$candidates" ]; then
        echo "No compressed logs older than 30 days in $archive"
        echo "Free space: $(free_space "$archive")"
        return 0
    fi
    count=$(printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | wc -l)
    bytes=$(printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | total_size)
    oldest=$(printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | oldest_date)
    echo "Archive:        $archive"
    echo "Files to purge: $count"
    echo "Space in use:   $(human_size "$bytes")"
    echo "Oldest log:     $oldest"
    printf '%s\n' "$candidates" | delete_files
    echo "Deleted $count file(s), reclaiming $(human_size "$bytes")"
    echo "Free space now: $(free_space "$archive")"
}

cleanup "${1:-/var/log/archive}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mail spool analyzer: per-message summary plus the most prolific sender.
set -uo pipefail

# Print the first value of the named header (headers end at the blank line).
get_header() {
    local file=$1 name=$2

    local raw=$1 angle
    angle=$(printf '%s\n' "$raw" | grep -o '<[^>]*>' | head -n 1)

    senders=$(mktemp)

        to=$(get_header "$file" 'To')
        subject=$(get_header "$file" 'Subject')

        recipient=$(extract_address "$to")

        printf '  from:        %s\n' "${sender:-unknown}"
        printf '  to:          %s\n' "${recipient:-unknown}"
        printf '  subject:     %s\n' "${subject:-(none)}"
        printf '  attachments: %s\n' "$attachments"
        printf '  bytes:       %s\n' "$bytes"
        [ -n "$sender" ] && printf '%s\n' "$sender" >> "$senders"
    done
    printf 'messages:    %d\n' "$count"
    top=$(sort "$senders" | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 1)
    rm -f "$senders"

        top_addr=$(awk '{print $2}' <<< "$top")
        top_n=$(awk '{print $1}' <<< "$top")
        printf 'top sender:  %s (%s messages)\n' "$top_addr" "$top_n"
    fi
}

text_es:
`track(process)`
Locates all active process identifiers matching the provided program name. For each identifier, determines the system user account running it. Retrieves the current resident set size memory allocated to it. Calculates the total combined memory usage across all matching instances. Identifies the single process identifier consuming the most memory. Extracts the full command line arguments used to launch that specific largest instance.
text_nat:
format_kb() {
    local kb=$1
    if [ "$kb" -ge 1048576 ]; then
        printf '%s GiB' "$(awk -v k="$kb" 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", k / 1048576 }')"
    elif [ "$kb" -ge 1024 ]; then
        printf '%s MiB' "$(awk -v k="$kb" 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", k / 1024 }')"
    else
        printf '%s KiB' "$kb"
    fi
}

find_pids() {
    pgrep -x -- "$1"
}

process_owner() {
    ps -o user= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '
}

process_rss() {
    ps -o rss= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '
}

process_cmdline() {
    if [ -r "/proc/$1/cmdline" ]; then
        tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$1/cmdline"
    else
        ps -o args= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

track() {
    local process=$1
    if [ -z "$process" ]; then
        echo "track: a program name is required" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    local pids
    pids=$(find_pids "$process")
    if [ -z "$pids" ]; then
        echo "No active processes named '$process'"
        return 1
    fi

    local pid owner rss total=0 count=0 top_pid= top_rss=0
    printf '%-8s %-12s %s\n' "PID" "USER" "RSS"
    for pid in $pids; do
        rss=$(process_rss "$pid")
        [ -n "$rss" ] || continue
        owner=$(process_owner "$pid")
        printf '%-8s %-12s %s\n' "$pid" "$owner" "$(format_kb "$rss")"
        total=$((total + rss))
        count=$((count + 1))
        if [ "$rss" -gt "$top_rss" ]; then
            top_rss=$rss
            top_pid=$pid
        fi
    done

    echo "Instances    : $count"
    echo "Total memory : $(format_kb "$total")"
    if [ -n "$top_pid" ]; then
        echo "Largest PID  : $top_pid ($(format_kb "$top_rss"))"
        echo "Command line : $(process_cmdline "$top_pid")"
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "usage: $(basename "$0") PROGRAM [PROGRAM ...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi

status=0
for name in "$@"; do
    track "$name" || status=$?
    echo
done
exit "$status"

`test(hosts)`
Reads a plain text list of network domain names. For each domain, queries the domain name system to retrieve its primary internet protocol address. Checks if a modern version six address is also available. Extracts the query response time in milliseconds. Looks up the registered organization name associated with the domain. Counts the total number of domains queried and the number that completely failed to resolve.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# DNS survey: resolve a list of domains and report address, IPv6 support,
# query time and registered organisation.
set -uo pipefail

DNS_TIMEOUT=3
ROW_FMT='%-28s %-16s %-5s %-8s %s\n'

trim() {
    sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' <<<"$1"
}

resolve_ipv4() {
    local answer
    answer=$(dig +time="$DNS_TIMEOUT" +tries=1 +short A "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    grep -m1 -E '^([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$' <<<"$answer"
}

has_ipv6() {
    local answer
    answer=$(dig +time="$DNS_TIMEOUT" +tries=1 +short AAAA "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    if grep -qm1 ':' <<<"$answer"; then
        echo yes
    else
        echo no
    fi
}

query_time_ms() {
    local response
    response=$(dig +time="$DNS_TIMEOUT" +tries=1 A "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    awk '/Query time:/ { print $4; exit }' <<<"$response"
}

org_name() {
    local record field
    record=$(whois "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    field=$(grep -im1 -E '^[[:space:]]*(Registrant )?Organi[sz]ation' <<<"$record")
    if [ -n "$field" ]; then
        trim "${field#*:}"
    else
        echo unknown
    fi
}

test() {
    local hosts=$1 line host addr v6 qtime org rate
    local total=0 failed=0
    [ -r "$hosts" ] || { echo "$hosts: cannot read host list" >&2; return 1; }
    printf "$ROW_FMT" HOST IPV4 IPV6 MS ORGANISATION
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        host=$(trim "$line")
        [ -n "$host" ] || continue
        case $host in \#*) continue ;; esac
        total=$((total + 1))
        addr=$(resolve_ipv4 "$host")
        if [ -z "$addr" ]; then
            failed=$((failed + 1))
            printf "$ROW_FMT" "$host" - - - unresolved
            continue
        fi
        v6=$(has_ipv6 "$host")
        qtime=$(query_time_ms "$host")
        org=$(org_name "$host")
        printf "$ROW_FMT" "$host" "$addr" "$v6" "${qtime:-n/a}" "${org:0:40}"
    done < "$hosts"
    rate=$(awk -v t="$total" -v f="$failed" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", t ? 100 * f / t : 0 }')
    printf '\n%d domain(s) queried, %d failed to resolve (%s%%)\n' "$total" "$failed" "$rate"
}

hosts=${1:-hosts.txt}
started=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
printf 'DNS survey of %s started %s\n\n' "$hosts" "$started"
test "$hosts"

text_es:
`compress(timeline)`
Processes a sequence log where each line begins with a numeric timestamp. Extracts the very first timestamp and the very last timestamp to calculate the original total duration. Calculates the time gap between each consecutive event. Identifies idle gaps that exceed a configured threshold and calculates an accumulated offset. Generates a compressed timeline file. Computes the new total duration after all large idle gaps are removed.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Compresses a timestamped sequence log by removing long idle gaps.

set -u

IDLE_THRESHOLD=${IDLE_THRESHOLD:-5.0}

first_timestamp() {
    head -n 1 "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
}

last_timestamp() {
    tail -n 1 "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
}

elapsed() {
    awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN { printf "%.3f", b - a }'
}

shift_back() {
    awk -v t="$1" -v off="$2" 'BEGIN { printf "%.3f", t - off }'
}

accumulate() {
    awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN { printf "%.3f", a + b }'
}

is_idle_gap() {
    awk -v g="$1" -v t="$IDLE_THRESHOLD" 'BEGIN { exit !(g > t) }'
}

compress() {
    local timeline=$1
    local output="${timeline%.*}.compressed.log"
    local start=$(first_timestamp "$timeline")
    local finish=$(last_timestamp "$timeline")
    local original=$(elapsed "$start" "$finish")
    local offset="0.000"
    local previous=$start
    local idle_count=0
    local timestamp rest gap moved

    : > "$output"
    while read -r timestamp rest; do
        gap=$(elapsed "$previous" "$timestamp")
        if is_idle_gap "$gap"; then
            offset=$(accumulate "$offset" "$gap")
            idle_count=$((idle_count + 1))
        fi
        moved=$(shift_back "$timestamp" "$offset")
        printf '%s %s\n' "$moved" "$rest" >> "$output"
        previous=$timestamp
    done < "$timeline"

    local new_start=$(first_timestamp "$output")
    local new_finish=$(last_timestamp "$output")
    local compressed=$(elapsed "$new_start" "$new_finish")
    printf 'compressed timeline: %s\n' "$output"
    printf 'idle gaps removed (> %ss): %d\n' "$IDLE_THRESHOLD" "$idle_count"
    printf 'original duration: %ss\n' "$original"
    printf 'new duration: %ss\n' "$compressed"
    printf 'time saved: %ss\n' "$offset"
}

main() {
    local program=$(basename "$0")
    if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s TIMELINE\n' "$program" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [ ! -s "$1" ]; then
        printf '%s: missing or empty timeline\n' "$1" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    compress "$1"
}

main "$@"

text_es: The entry function `preprocess(image)` evaluates a disk image before analysis. Given a disk image file, find its absolute path, calculate the md5 checksum, calculate the sha256 checksum, get the file size in bytes, extract the image creation date, count the number of strings longer than ten characters, find the starting offset of the first boot sector, and extract the operating system label. Return a space separated text line with these extracted fields.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Disk image preprocessing module: extracts identifying metadata from an image.

set -o pipefail

abs_path() {
    local image=$1
    local dir
    dir=$(dirname -- "$image")
    dir=$(cd -- "$dir" && pwd -P)
    local base
    base=$(basename -- "$image")
    printf '%s/%s\n' "$dir" "$base"
}

md5_sum() {
    local out
    out=$(md5sum -- "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "${out%% *}"
}

sha256_sum() {
    local out
    out=$(sha256sum -- "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "${out%% *}"
}

file_size() {
    stat -c '%s' -- "$1"
}

creation_date() {
    local birth
    birth=$(stat -c '%w' -- "$1")
    if [ "$birth" = "-" ] || [ -z "$birth" ]; then
        birth=$(stat -c '%y' -- "$1")
    fi
    date -d "$birth" -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
}

long_string_count() {
    LC_ALL=C strings -n 11 -- "$1" | wc -l
}

boot_sector_offset() {
    local hit off
    while IFS= read -r hit; do
        off=${hit%%:*}
        if [ "$off" -ge 510 ] && [ $(( (off - 510) % 512 )) -eq 0 ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$(( off - 510 ))"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(LC_ALL=C grep -aboP '\x55\xaa' -- "$1")
    printf 'NONE\n'
}

os_label() {
    local label
    label=$(LC_ALL=C strings -n 4 -- "$1" | grep -m1 -oE 'MSWIN4\.[01]|NTFS    |EXFAT   |FAT(12|16|32) *|GRUB|LILO|Linux|Darwin|FreeBSD')
    if [ -z "$label" ]; then
        label='UNKNOWN'
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${label// /}"
}

preprocess() {
    local image=$1
    if [ ! -f "$image" ] || [ ! -r "$image" ]; then
        printf 'preprocess: cannot read image: %s\n' "$image" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local path md5 sha size created strings_count offset label
    path=$(abs_path "$image")
    md5=$(md5_sum "$image")
    sha=$(sha256_sum "$image")
    size=$(file_size "$image")
    created=$(creation_date "$image")
    strings_count=$(long_string_count "$image")
    offset=$(boot_sector_offset "$image")
    label=$(os_label "$image")
    printf '%s %s %s %s %s %s %s %s\n' \
        "$path" "$md5" "$sha" "$size" "$created" \
        "$strings_count" "$offset" "$label"
}

main() {
    local prog
    prog=$(basename -- "$0")
    if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s IMAGE [IMAGE...]\n' "$prog" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    local image status=0
    for image in "$@"; do
        preprocess "$image" || status=1
    done
    return "$status"
}

main "$@"

    local out
    out=`md5sum -- "$1"`
    printf '%s\n' "${out%% *}"
}

sha256_sum() {
    local out
    out=`sha256sum -- "$1"`
    printf '%s\n' "${out%% *}"
}

file_size() {
    stat -c '%s' -- "$1"
}

creation_date() {
    local birth
    birth=`stat -c '%w' -- "$1"`
    if [ "$birth" = "-" ] || [ -z "$birth" ]; then
        birth=`stat -c '%y' -- "$1"`
    fi
    date -d "$birth" -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
}

long_string_count() {
    LC_ALL=C strings -n 11 -- "$1" | wc -l
}

boot_sector_offset() {
    local hit off
    while IFS= read -r hit; do
        off=${hit%%:*}
        if [ "$off" -ge 510 ] && [ $(( (off - 510) % 512 )) -eq 0 ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$(( off - 510 ))"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(LC_ALL=C grep -aboP '\x55\xaa' -- "$1")
    printf 'NONE\n'
}

os_label() {
    local label
    label=`LC_ALL=C strings -n 4 -- "$1" | grep -m1 -oE 'MSWIN4\.[01]|NTFS    |EXFAT   |FAT(12|16|32) *|GRUB|LILO|Linux|Darwin|FreeBSD'`
    if [ -z "$label" ]; then
        label='UNKNOWN'
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${label// /}"
}

preprocess() {
    local image=$1
    if [ ! -f "$image" ] || [ ! -r "$image" ]; then
        printf 'preprocess: cannot read image: %s\n' "$image" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    local path md5 sha size created strings_count offset label
    path=`abs_path "$image"`
    md5=`md5_sum "$image"`
    sha=`sha256_sum "$image"`
    size=`file_size "$image"`
    created=`creation_date "$image"`
    strings_count=`long_string_count "$image"`
    offset=`boot_sector_offset "$image"`
    label=`os_label "$image"`
    printf '%s %s %s %s %s %s %s %s\n' \
        "$path" "$md5" "$sha" "$size" "$created" \
        "$strings_count" "$offset" "$label"
}

main() {
    local prog
    prog=`basename -- "$0"`
    if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s IMAGE [IMAGE...]\n' "$prog" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    local image status=0
    for image in "$@"; do
        preprocess "$image" || status=1
    done
    return "$status"
}

main "$@"

Given a target endpoint, perform a curl request to get the http status code, get the total response time, extract the response content type, get the payload size in bytes, get the server header string, count the number of json keys returned, compute the base64 encoding of the body, and extract the date header. Return a list of these performance metrics.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Simple HTTP benchmark module: collects performance metrics for a target URL.
set -uo pipefail

fetch_target() {
    local url=$1 dir=$2
    curl -s -S -L -D "$dir/headers" -o "$dir/body" \
        -w '%{http_code}\t%{time_total}\t%{content_type}\t%{size_download}\n' \
        "$url" >"$dir/meta" 2>"$dir/error"
}

meta_field() {
    cut -f"$1" "$2/meta"
}

header_value() {
    local name=$1 file=$2 line
    line=$(grep -i "^${name}:" "$file" | tail -n 1)
    printf '%s' "${line#*: }" | tr -d '\r'
}

json_key_count() {
    local file=$1 count
    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        count=$(jq 'if type == "object" then (keys | length) elif type == "array" then length else 0 end' "$file" 2>/dev/null)
        printf '%s' "${count:-0}"
    else
        count=$(grep -o '"[^"]*"[[:space:]]*:' "$file" | wc -l)
        printf '%s' "${count// /}"
    fi
}

body_base64() {
    base64 "$1" | tr -d '\n'
}

benchmark() {
    local url=$1 dir status elapsed ctype size server keys encoded date_hdr
    dir=$(mktemp -d)
    if ! fetch_target "$url" "$dir"; then
        printf 'benchmark: request failed: %s\n' "$(tr -d '\r' <"$dir/error")" >&2
        rm -rf "$dir"
        return 1
    fi
    status=$(meta_field 1 "$dir")
    elapsed=$(meta_field 2 "$dir")
    ctype=$(meta_field 3 "$dir")
    size=$(meta_field 4 "$dir")
    server=$(header_value "Server" "$dir/headers")
    date_hdr=$(header_value "Date" "$dir/headers")
    keys=$(json_key_count "$dir/body")
    encoded=$(body_base64 "$dir/body")
    rm -rf "$dir"

    printf 'http_status=%s\n' "$status"
    printf 'response_time=%s\n' "$elapsed"
    printf 'content_type=%s\n' "${ctype:-unknown}"
    printf 'payload_bytes=%s\n' "$size"
    printf 'server=%s\n' "${server:-unknown}"
    printf 'json_keys=%s\n' "$keys"
    printf 'body_base64=%s\n' "$encoded"
    printf 'date=%s\n' "${date_hdr:-unknown}"
}

main() {
    local url rc=0
    for url in "${@:-https://httpbin.org/get}"; do
        printf '=== %s (measured at %s) ===\n' "$url" "$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
        benchmark "$url" || rc=1
    done
    return "$rc"
}

main "$@"

Given a project directory containing a build script, extract the minimum required version, find the project name, count the number of added executables, count the number of added libraries, extract the c++ standard level, count the number of target link libraries, find the output binary name, and calculate the total line count of the build file. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Review a compilation environment described by a CMake build script.
set -uo pipefail

build_file() {
    local dir=$1 candidate
    for candidate in CMakeLists.txt cmake/CMakeLists.txt src/CMakeLists.txt; do
        if [[ -f "$dir/$candidate" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$dir/$candidate"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

minimum_version() {
    local line
    line=$(grep -im1 'cmake_minimum_required' "$1")
    local version
    version=$(sed -nE 's/.*VERSION[[:space:]]+([0-9][0-9.]*).*/\1/Ip' <<<"$line")
    printf '%s\n' "${version:-unknown}"
}

project_name() {
    local name
    name=$(sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*project[[:space:]]*\([[:space:]]*"?([A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+).*/\1/Ip' "$1" | head -n1)
    printf '%s\n' "${name:-unknown}"
}

count_command() {
    grep -ciE "^[[:space:]]*$2[[:space:]]*\(" "$1"
}

cxx_standard() {
    local standard
    standard=$(sed -nE 's/.*CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD[[:space:]]+([0-9]+).*/\1/p' "$1" | head -n1)
    if [[ -z $standard ]]; then
        standard=$(sed -nE 's/.*-std=(gnu|c)\+\+([0-9a-z]+).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -n1)
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${standard:-unspecified}"
}

output_binary() {
    local target
    target=$(sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*add_executable[[:space:]]*\([[:space:]]*([A-Za-z0-9_.${}-]+).*/\1/Ip' "$1" | head -n1)
    printf '%s\n' "${target:-none}"
}

evaluate() {
    local dir=$1 file
    file=$(build_file "$dir") || { echo "evaluate: no build script under $dir" >&2; return 1; }
    local details=()
    details+=("minimum_version=$(minimum_version "$file")")
    details+=("project=$(project_name "$file")")
    details+=("executables=$(count_command "$file" add_executable)")
    details+=("libraries=$(count_command "$file" add_library)")
    details+=("cxx_standard=$(cxx_standard "$file")")
    details+=("link_libraries=$(count_command "$file" target_link_libraries)")
    details+=("output_binary=$(output_binary "$file")")
    details+=("total_lines=$(wc -l <"$file")")
    printf '%s\n' "${details[@]}"
}

main() {
    local target=${1:-.} report entry absolute
    if [[ ! -d $target ]]; then
        echo "evaluate: $target is not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    report=$(evaluate "$target") || return 1
    absolute=$(cd "$target" && pwd)
    printf 'Build configuration for %s\n' "${absolute##*/}"
    while IFS= read -r entry; do
        printf '  %s\n' "$entry"
    done <<<"$report"
}

if [[ ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} == "$0" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Collect metrics about a Django-style project workspace.
set -uo pipefail

find_settings() {
    find "$1" -type f -name settings.py 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
}

count_installed_apps() {
    local settings=$1 block
    [ -f "$settings" ] || { echo 0; return; }
    block=$(sed -n '/INSTALLED_APPS[[:space:]]*=/,/^]/p' "$settings")
    grep -cE "^[[:space:]]*['\"]" <<<"$block"
}

count_models() {
    grep -rhE "^[[:space:]]*class[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(.*Model" \
        --include='models*.py' "$1" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

count_views() {
    grep -rhE "^[[:space:]]*(def|class)[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_]" \
        --include='views*.py' "$1" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

count_templates() {
    find "$1" -type f -path '*templates*' \( -name '*.html' -o -name '*.txt' \) \
        2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

framework_version() {
    local version
    version=$(django-admin --version 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -z "$version" ]; then
        version=$(grep -ihoE "django[[:space:]]*[=><~]+[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9.]*" \
            "$1"/requirements*.txt 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | grep -oE '[0-9][0-9.]*')
    fi
    echo "${version:-unknown}"
}

count_migrations() {
    local db count=""
    db=$(find "$1" -type f -name '*.sqlite3' 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
    if [ -n "$db" ] && command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        count=$(sqlite3 "$db" 'select count(*) from django_migrations;' 2>/dev/null)
    fi
    if [ -z "$count" ]; then
        count=$(find "$1" -type f -path '*migrations*' -name '[0-9]*.py' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    fi
    echo "$count"
}

database_engine() {
    local engine
    engine=$(grep -oE "'ENGINE'[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*'[^']+'" "$1" 2>/dev/null |
        head -n 1 | awk -F"'" '{print $4}')
    echo "${engine:-unknown}"
}

count_python_lines() {
    find "$1" -type f -name '*.py' -exec cat {} + 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

collect() {
    local directory=$1 settings
    settings=$(find_settings "$directory")
    printf '%s %s %s %s %s %s %s %s\n' \
        "$(count_installed_apps "$settings")" \
        "$(count_models "$directory")" \
        "$(count_views "$directory")" \
        "$(count_templates "$directory")" \
        "$(framework_version "$directory")" \
        "$(count_migrations "$directory")" \
        "$(database_engine "$settings")" \
        "$(count_python_lines "$directory")"
}

main() {
    local directory=${1:-.} i
    if [ ! -d "$directory" ]; then
        echo "collect: $directory: not a directory" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    local labels=(installed_apps models views templates framework_version
        applied_migrations database_engine python_lines)
    local -a metrics
    read -r -a metrics <<<"$(collect "$directory")"
    for i in "${!labels[@]}"; do
        printf '%-20s %s\n' "${labels[i]}" "${metrics[i]}"
    done
}

main "$@"

Given a block cache device path, get the current cache mode, extract the cache state string, get the dirty data size in megabytes, get the clean data size in megabytes, count the number of writeback operations, find the read hit ratio percentage, get the bypass hit ratio percentage, and extract the device hardware sector size. Output these storage metrics in a list.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inspect bcache (block layer cache) devices through their sysfs attributes.
set -uo pipefail

read_attr() {
    [ -r "$1" ] || return 1
    tr -d '\0' < "$1"
}

first_attr() {
    local file value
    for file in "$@"; do
        value=$(read_attr "$file") || continue
        if [ -n "$value" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$value"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

resolve_base() {
    local base
    base=$(readlink -f "$1") || return 1
    case $base in
        /sys/*) ;;
        *) base=/sys/block/$(basename "$base") ;;
    esac
    [ -d "$base/bcache" ] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$base"
}

cache_mode() {
    local raw mode
    raw=$(first_attr "$1/bcache/cache_mode") || return 1
    mode=${raw#*[}
    [ "$mode" = "$raw" ] || mode=${mode%%]*}
    printf '%s\n' "$mode"
}

to_mb() {
    awk -v s="$1" 'BEGIN {
        if (match(s, /[A-Za-z]$/)) { u = substr(s, RSTART); s = substr(s, 1, RSTART - 1) } else u = "B"
        if (u == "k" || u == "K") f = 1 / 1024
        else if (u == "M") f = 1
        else if (u == "G") f = 1024
        else if (u == "T") f = 1048576
        else f = 1 / 1048576
        printf "%.1f\n", s * f
    }'
}

dirty_mb() {
    local raw
    raw=$(first_attr "$1/bcache/dirty_data") || return 1
    to_mb "$raw"
}

cache_capacity_mb() {
    local bucket nbuckets bucket_mb
    bucket=$(first_attr "$1/bcache/cache/cache0/bucket_size") || return 1
    nbuckets=$(first_attr "$1/bcache/cache/cache0/nbuckets") || return 1
    bucket_mb=$(to_mb "$bucket")
    awk -v b="$bucket_mb" -v n="$nbuckets" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f\n", b * n }'
}

clean_mb() {
    local raw total dirty

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inspect bcache (block layer cache) devices through their sysfs attributes.
set -uo pipefail

read_attr() {
    [ -r "$1" ] || return 1
    tr -d '\0' < "$1"
}

first_attr() {
    local file value
    for file in "$@"; do
        value=`read_attr "$file"` || continue
        if [ -n "$value" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$value"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

resolve_base() {
    local base
    base=`readlink -f "$1"` || return 1
    case $base in
        /sys/*) ;;
        *) base=/sys/block/`basename "$base"` ;;
    esac
    [ -d "$base/bcache" ] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$base"
}

cache_mode() {
    local raw mode
    raw=`first_attr "$1/bcache/cache_mode"` || return 1
    mode=${raw#*[}
    [ "$mode" = "$raw" ] || mode=${mode%%]*}
    printf '%s\n' "$mode"
}

to_mb() {
    awk -v s="$1" 'BEGIN {
        if (match(s, /[A-Za-z]$/)) { u = substr(s, RSTART); s = substr(s, 1, RSTART - 1) } else u = "B"
        if (u == "k" || u == "K") f = 1 / 1024
        else if (u == "M") f = 1
        else if (u == "G") f = 1024
        else if (u == "T") f = 1048576
        else f = 1 / 1048576
        printf "%.1f\n", s * f
    }'
}

dirty_mb() {
    local raw
    raw=`first_attr "$1/bcache/dirty_data"` || return 1

cache_capacity_mb() {

Given a cluster node address, get the node identifier, get its current role as leader or follower, count the number of connected replicas, get the configured cluster epoch, count the number of assigned hash slots, get the count of failover attempts, measure the network round trip ping time, and extract the version string of the running service. The script processes a folder of audio files to apply volume normalization. For each file, the entry function `normalize(directory)` must extract the base filename, extract the file extension, find the current peak volume level, find the mean volume level, calculate the required gain adjustment, determine the audio sample rate, get the duration in seconds, and grab the current date for a logging prefix. It then applies the gain adjustment to create a new normalized audio file and calculates the new file size. Finally, it outputs a summary report printing the extracted filename, extension, original peak, mean volume, gain adjustment, sample rate, duration, date, and the new file size. Example input could be a directory with a single audio file. Example output would be a sentence stating the file was normalized from a peak of minus five decibels with all gathered metrics included.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Batch volume normalization of an audio folder using ffmpeg/ffprobe.

set -u

TARGET_PEAK="-1.0"

volume_stats() {
    local report peak mean
    report=$(ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostdin -i "$1" -af volumedetect -f null /dev/null 2>&1)
    peak=$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | awk -F': ' '/max_volume/ {print $2}' | tr -d ' dB')
    mean=$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | awk -F': ' '/mean_volume/ {print $2}' | tr -d ' dB')
    printf '%s %s\n' "${peak:-0.0}" "${mean:-0.0}"
}

gain_for_peak() {
    awk -v peak="$1" -v target="$TARGET_PEAK" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", target - peak }'
}

sample_rate() {
    ffprobe -v error -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=sample_rate \
        -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$1"
}

duration_seconds() {
    local raw
    raw=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration \
        -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$1")
    awk -v d="$raw" 'BEGIN { printf "%.0f", d }'
}

apply_gain() {
    ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostdin -loglevel error -y -i "$1" \
        -af "volume=${2}dB" "$3"
}

human_size() {
    local bytes
    bytes=$(stat -c '%s' "$1" 2>/dev/null || stat -f '%z' "$1")
    awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f KiB", b / 1024 }'
}

normalize() {
    local directory="$1" file base ext stamp stats peak mean gain rate duration target size
    stamp=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d')
    for file in "$directory"/*.[Mm][Pp]3 "$directory"/*.[Ww][Aa][Vv] "$directory"/*.[Ff][Ll][Aa][Cc]; do
        [ -f "$file" ] || continue
        base=$(basename -- "$file")
        ext="${base##*.}"
        stats=$(volume_stats "$file")
        read -r peak mean <<<"$stats"
        gain=$(gain_for_peak "$peak")
        rate=$(sample_rate "$file")
        duration=$(duration_seconds "$file")
        target="$directory/normalized-${base%.*}.$ext"
        apply_gain "$file" "$gain" "$target" || continue
        size=$(human_size "$target")
        echo "[$stamp] Normalized $base (.$ext) from a peak of ${peak} dB" \
             "(mean ${mean} dB) with a gain of ${gain} dB at ${rate} Hz," \
             "${duration}s long; new file size is $size."
    done
}

main() {
    local directory="${1:-.}"
    if [ ! -d "$directory" ]; then
        echo "normalize: '$directory' is not a directory" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    normalize "$directory"
}

main "$@"

text_es: The script processes a folder of high resolution pictures and generates smaller thumbnails. For every picture, the logic in `thumbnail(folder)` must extract the base filename without the extension, extract the original file extension, find the original image width in pixels, find the original image height, calculate the new thumbnail width as exactly half the original, calculate the new thumbnail height as exactly half, get the original file size in bytes, generate a timestamp to append to the thumbnail name, and finally get the generated thumbnail file size. The script uses these values to resize the picture and prints a report line for each processed picture containing the filename, extension, original width, original height, new width, new height, original size, timestamp, and new size. Example input is a folder with one picture. Example output is a string stating the picture was resized from two thousand pixels to one thousand pixels alongside the sizes.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generate half-size thumbnails for every picture in a folder and report on each.

set -u

thumbnail() {
    local folder="$1"
    local outdir="$folder/thumbs"

    if [ ! -d "$folder" ]; then
        echo "thumbnail: '$folder' is not a directory" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    mkdir -p "$outdir"

    local picture
    for picture in "$folder"/*.[jJ][pP][gG] "$folder"/*.[jJ][pP][eE][gG] \
                   "$folder"/*.[pP][nN][gG] "$folder"/*.[gG][iI][fF]; do
        [ -f "$picture" ] || continue

        local base=$(basename "$picture")
        local name="${base%.*}"
        local ext="${base##*.}"

        local width=$(identify -format '%w' "$picture")
        local height=$(identify -format '%h' "$picture")
        local new_width=$(( width / 2 ))
        local new_height=$(( height / 2 ))
        local old_size=$(stat -c '%s' "$picture")
        local stamp=$(date '+%Y%m%d%H%M%S')

        local thumb="$outdir/${name}_${stamp}.${ext}"
        if ! convert "$picture" -resize "${new_width}x${new_height}!" "$thumb"; then
            echo "thumbnail: failed to resize $base" >&2
            continue
        fi

        local new_size=$(stat -c '%s' "$thumb")
        report_line "$name" "$ext" "$width" "$height" "$new_width" \
                    "$new_height" "$old_size" "$stamp" "$new_size"
    done
}

report_line() {
    local name="$1" ext="$2" width="$3" height="$4"
    local new_width="$5" new_height="$6" old_size="$7" stamp="$8" new_size="$9"

    local old_human=$(human_size "$old_size")
    local new_human=$(human_size "$new_size")

    printf '%s.%s: resized from %sx%s px (%s) to %sx%s px (%s) as %s_%s.%s\n' \
        "$name" "$ext" "$width" "$height" "$old_human" \
        "$new_width" "$new_height" "$new_human" "$name" "$stamp" "$ext"
}

human_size() {
    local bytes="$1"
    if [ "$bytes" -ge 1048576 ]; then
        local mb=$(awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", b / 1048576 }')
        echo "${mb}MB"
    elif [ "$bytes" -ge 1024 ]; then
        local kb=$(awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", b / 1024 }')
        echo "${kb}KB"
    else
        echo "${bytes}B"
    fi
}

main() {
    local folder="${1:-pictures}"
    thumbnail "$folder" || return 1

    local made=$(find "$folder/thumbs" -type f | wc -l)
    echo "Done: $made thumbnail(s) in $folder/thumbs"
}

main "$@"

text_es: The script generates a secure connection configuration file based on a list of target hostnames. For each host, the `configure(hosts)` routine must resolve the hostname to its numeric internet protocol address, determine the average network latency to the host, find the operating system type of the remote host, generate a secure random key name, retrieve the local current username, get the local machine hostname, determine the current system year for a copyright header, and find the total number of active network interfaces on the local machine. It creates a configuration block for each host and prints a sentence confirming the setup including the numeric address, latency, operating system, key name, local user, local host, year, and interface count. Example input is a file containing a list of domains. Example output is a configuration block followed by a sentence confirming generation with all variables.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generates a secure connection configuration file from a list of target hosts.
set -uo pipefail

resolve_ip() {
    local host=$1 ip
    ip=$(getent ahostsv4 "$host" | awk '{ print $1; exit }')
    if [ -z "$ip" ]; then
        ip=$(dig +short A "$host" | head -n 1)
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${ip:-unresolved}"
}

avg_latency() {
    local host=$1 summary avg
    summary=$(ping -c 3 -W 2 "$host" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
    avg=$(printf '%s\n' "$summary" | awk -F'/' '/min\/avg/ { printf "%.1f", $5 }')
    printf '%s\n' "${avg:-0.0}"
}

remote_os() {
    local host=$1 os
    os=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 "$host" uname -s 2>/dev/null)
    printf '%s\n' "${os:-unknown}"
}

gen_key_name() {
    local entropy
    entropy=$(head -c 12 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9')
    printf 'id_%s\n' "$entropy"
}

count_interfaces() {
    ls /sys/class/net | wc -l
}

configure() {
    local hosts=("$@")
    local user localhost year ifaces host ip latency os key
    user=$(id -un)
    localhost=$(hostname)
    year=$(date +%Y)
    ifaces=$(count_interfaces)

    printf '# Copyright (c) %s %s. Generated on %s.\n\n' "$year" "$user" "$localhost"
    for host in "${hosts[@]}"; do
        ip=$(resolve_ip "$host")
        latency=$(avg_latency "$host")
        os=$(remote_os "$host")
        key=$(gen_key_name)
        printf 'Host %s\n' "$host"
        printf '    HostName %s\n' "$ip"
        printf '    User %s\n' "$user"
        printf '    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/%s\n' "$key"
        printf '    ConnectTimeout %s\n' "${latency%%.*}"
        printf '    # remote os: %s\n\n' "$os"
        printf 'Configured %s at %s (%s ms avg, %s) with key %s for %s@%s, %s, %s interfaces.\n\n' \
            "$host" "$ip" "$latency" "$os" "$key" "$user" "$localhost" "$year" "$ifaces"
    done
}

main() {
    local file=${1:-hosts.txt} hosts total
    if [ ! -r "$file" ]; then
        printf '%s: cannot read host list\n' "$file" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    mapfile -t hosts < <(grep -Ev '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$file")
    total=$(printf '%s\n' "${hosts[@]}" | grep -c .)
    if [ "$total" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf '%s: no hosts listed\n' "$file" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    configure "${hosts[@]}"
}

main "$@"

        printf '    ConnectTimeout %s\n' "${latency%%.*}"

main() {
    local file=${1:-hosts.txt} hosts total
    if [ ! -r "$file" ]; then
        printf '%s: cannot read host list\n' "$file" >&2

    fi

text_es: The script analyzes a specific storage drive device and provides a detailed capacity and hardware report. The `analyze(device)` entry must retrieve the universal unique identifier of the primary partition, find the file system type used on that partition, determine the total storage capacity, find the currently used storage space, calculate the available free space, retrieve the hardware serial number of the drive, determine the device rotational speed or solid state status, get the sector size of the device, and find the current mount point path if it exists. The script prints a comprehensive summary sentence incorporating all these hardware and capacity details. Example input is a device path like dev sda. Example output is a sentence stating a solid state drive with a specific serial number has fifty gigabytes free out of one hundred total reporting all properties.
text_nat:
set -u

primary_partition() {
    local device="$1"
    local part
    part=$(lsblk -nrpo NAME,TYPE "$device" | awk '$2=="part"{print $1; exit}')
    if [ -z "$part" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$device"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$part"
    fi
}

partition_uuid() {
    local uuid
    uuid=$(lsblk -ndo UUID "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "${uuid:-unset}"
}

filesystem_type() {
    local fstype
    fstype=$(lsblk -ndo FSTYPE "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "${fstype:-unknown}"
}

total_capacity() {
    lsblk -bndo SIZE "$1"
}

mount_point() {
    local mnt
    mnt=$(lsblk -ndo MOUNTPOINT "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "${mnt:-none}"
}

used_space() {
    local mnt="$1"
    if [ "$mnt" = "none" ]; then
        printf '0\n'
    else
        df -B1 --output=used "$mnt" | tail -n 1 | tr -d ' '
    fi
}

serial_number() {
    local serial
    serial=$(lsblk -ndo SERIAL "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "${serial:-unavailable}"
}

media_type() {
    local name rota
    name=$(basename "$1")
    rota=$(cat "/sys/block/$name/queue/rotational" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$rota" = "0" ]; then
        printf 'solid state drive\n'
    else
        printf 'rotational drive\n'
    fi
}

sector_size() {
    lsblk -ndo PHY-SEC "$1"
}

to_gb() {
    awk -v b="$1" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f", b / 1000000000 }'
}

analyze() {
    local device="$1" part uuid fstype total mnt used free media serial sector
    if [ ! -b "$device" ]; then
        printf '%s is not a block device\n' "$device" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    part=$(primary_partition "$device")
    uuid=$(partition_uuid "$part")
    fstype=$(filesystem_type "$part")
    total=$(total_capacity "$device")
    mnt=$(mount_point "$part")
    used=$(used_space "$mnt")
    free=$(( total - used ))
    media=$(media_type "$device")
    serial=$(serial_number "$device")
    sector=$(sector_size "$device")
    printf 'Device %s is a %s with serial %s, sector size %s bytes, ' \
        "$device" "$media" "$serial" "$sector"
    printf 'whose primary partition %s (UUID %s) is formatted as %s ' \
        "$part" "$uuid" "$fstype"
    printf 'and mounted at %s, using %s GB ' \
        "$mnt" "$(to_gb "$used")"
    printf 'and leaving %s GB free out of ' \
        "$(to_gb "$free")"
    printf '%s GB total.\n' "$(to_gb "$total")"
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s /dev/sda\n' "$(basename "$0")" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    analyze "$1"
}

main "$@"

The script examines a compressed backup archive to ensure its contents are valid and uncorrupted. The `verify(archive)` function needs to calculate the message digest checksum of the archive file, determine the total size of the compressed archive in bytes, count the total number of files contained within the archive, find the name of the largest file inside the archive, extract the uncompressed size of that largest file, retrieve the archive modification timestamp, find the current available disk space in the temporary extraction directory, calculate the compression ratio, and determine the operating system architecture. It prints a verification report detailing the archive checksum, compressed size, file count, largest file name, uncompressed size, timestamp, free space, compression ratio, and architecture. Example input is a path to a compressed archive file. Example output is a sentence confirming the backup contains one hundred files and includes all other metrics.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify a compressed tar archive and report its metadata.

set -o pipefail

TMPDIR_EXTRACT="${TMPDIR_EXTRACT:-/tmp}"

human_bytes() {
    local bytes=$1
    awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN {
        split("B KiB MiB GiB TiB", u, " ")
        i = 1
        while (b >= 1024 && i < 5) { b /= 1024; i++ }
        printf (i == 1 ? "%d %s" : "%.2f %s"), b, u[i]
    }'
}

archive_checksum() {
    local archive=$1
    local line
    line=$(sha256sum -- "$archive")
    printf '%s\n' "${line%% *}"
}

largest_entry() {
    # Prints "<uncompressed-size> <name>" for the biggest member.
    local archive=$1
    tar -tvf "$archive" 2>/dev/null |
        awk '$0 !~ /\/$/ { size=$3; name=$NF; if (size+0 > max+0) { max=size; best=name } }
             END { if (best != "") print max, best }'
}

compression_ratio() {
    local compressed=$1 uncompressed=$2
    awk -v c="$compressed" -v u="$uncompressed" \
        'BEGIN { if (c > 0) printf "%.2f", u / c; else print "0.00" }'
}

verify() {
    local archive=$1

    if [[ ! -f $archive ]]; then
        printf 'verify: %s: no such archive\n' "$archive" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local checksum
    checksum=$(archive_checksum "$archive")
    local compressed_size
    compressed_size=$(stat -c %s -- "$archive")
    local file_count
    file_count=$(tar -tf "$archive" 2>/dev/null | grep -vc '/$')
    local biggest
    biggest=$(largest_entry "$archive")
    local largest_name=${biggest#* }
    local largest_size=${biggest%% *}
    local timestamp
    timestamp=$(stat -c %y -- "$archive")
    local free_space
    free_space=$(df -B1 --output=avail "$TMPDIR_EXTRACT" | tail -n 1 | tr -d ' ')
    local uncompressed_total
    uncompressed_total=$(tar -tvf "$archive" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ s += $3 } END { print s+0 }')
    local ratio
    ratio=$(compression_ratio "$compressed_size" "$uncompressed_total")
    local arch
    arch=$(uname -m)

    printf 'Verification report for %s\n' "$archive"
    printf '  checksum (sha256): %s\n' "$checksum"
    printf '  compressed size:   %s\n' "$(human_bytes "$compressed_size")"
    printf '  files contained:   %s\n' "$file_count"
    printf '  largest file:      %s\n' "$largest_name"
    printf '  its size:          %s\n' "$(human_bytes "$largest_size")"
    printf '  modified:          %s\n' "$timestamp"
    printf '  free space in %s: %s\n' "$TMPDIR_EXTRACT" "$(human_bytes "$free_space")"
    printf '  compression ratio: %sx\n' "$ratio"
    printf '  architecture:      %s\n' "$arch"
    printf 'The backup contains %d files, %s compressed (%sx), largest is %s.\n' \
        "$file_count" "$(human_bytes "$compressed_size")" "$ratio" "$largest_name"
}

verify "${1:?usage: $(basename "$0") ARCHIVE}"

The script outputs a report detailing the data file size, row count, database engine version, initial database size, final database size, date, user identifier, and import duration. Example input is a path to a text file. Example output is a summary of the data insertion process with all gathered metrics.
text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ingest a raw text data file into a local SQLite database and report metrics.

set -u

DB_FILE="${DB_FILE:-./ingest.db}"
TABLE="records"

file_size() {
    local path="$1"
    if [ -f "$path" ]; then
        stat -c %s "$path"
    else
        echo 0
    fi
}

row_count() {
    grep -c '[^[:space:]]' "$1"
}

engine_version() {
    sqlite3 --version | awk '{print $1}'
}

prepare_db() {
    sqlite3 "$DB_FILE" "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS $TABLE (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, line TEXT);"
}

insert_rows() {
    local datafile="$1"
    {
        echo "BEGIN;"
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            printf "INSERT INTO %s (line) VALUES ('%s');\n" "$TABLE" "${line//\'/\'\'}"
        done < "$datafile"
        echo "COMMIT;"
    } | sqlite3 "$DB_FILE"
}

import() {
    local datafile="$1"
    if [ ! -r "$datafile" ]; then
        echo "import: cannot read '$datafile'" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local bytes=$(file_size "$datafile")
    local rows=$(row_count "$datafile")
    local version=$(engine_version)
    prepare_db
    local size_before=$(file_size "$DB_FILE")
    local started=$(date +%s)

    insert_rows "$datafile" || return 1

    local finished=$(date +%s)
    local elapsed=$(( finished - started ))
    local size_after=$(file_size "$DB_FILE")
    local stamp=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
    local who=$(id -un)
    local uid=$(id -u)

    printf 'Import report for %s\n' "$datafile"
    printf '  data file size : %s bytes\n' "$bytes"
    printf '  rows imported  : %s\n' "$rows"
    printf '  sqlite version : %s\n' "$version"
    printf '  db size before : %s bytes\n' "$size_before"
    printf '  db size after  : %s bytes\n' "$size_after"
    printf '  date           : %s\n' "$stamp"
    printf '  user           : %s (uid %s)\n' "$who" "$uid"
    printf '  duration       : %s seconds\n' "$elapsed"
}

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "usage: $(basename "$0") DATAFILE" >&2
    exit 2
fi
import "$1"

The `evict(instance)` logic must retrieve the specific version of the data store software, determine the total amount of memory currently used by the data store, find the total number of keys stored in the database, extract the system uptime of the data store service in seconds, determine the number of currently connected client applications, retrieve the configured maximum memory limit, get the network port the instance is listening on, measure the exact duration in milliseconds it takes to clear the keys, and find the hostname of the server. The script prints a report confirming the software version, memory used, key count, system uptime, client count, memory limit, network port, execution duration, and server hostname. text_nat:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Controlled clearing (eviction) of an in-memory data store instance.
set -uo pipefail

REDIS_CLI=${REDIS_CLI:-redis-cli}

parse_host() {
    local instance=$1
    printf '%s\n' "${instance%%:*}"
}

parse_port() {
    local instance=$1
    case $instance in
        *:*) printf '%s\n' "${instance##*:}" ;;
        *)   printf '%s\n' "6379" ;;
    esac
}

rs() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    shift 2
    "$REDIS_CLI" -h "$host" -p "$port" "$@" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
}

info_field() {
    local host=$1 port=$2 field=$3
    local raw
    raw=$(rs "$host" "$port" INFO ALL)
    printf '%s\n' "$raw" | awk -F: -v key="$field" '$1 == key { print $2; exit }'
}

key_count() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    local size
    size=$(rs "$host" "$port" DBSIZE)
    printf '%s\n' "${size:-0}"
}

configured_maxmemory() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    local pair
    pair=$(rs "$host" "$port" CONFIG GET maxmemory)
    printf '%s\n' "$(printf '%s\n' "$pair" | sed -n '2p')"
}

flush_duration_ms() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    local start end
    start=$(date +%s%3N)
    rs "$host" "$port" FLUSHDB >/dev/null
    end=$(date +%s%3N)
    printf '%s\n' "$(( end - start ))"
}

evict() {
    local instance=$1
    local host port
    host=$(parse_host "$instance")
    port=$(parse_port "$instance")

    if [ "$(rs "$host" "$port" PING)" != "PONG" ]; then
        printf 'Cannot reach data store instance %s\n' "$instance" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local version memory keys uptime clients limit duration server
    version=$(info_field "$host" "$port" redis_version)
    memory=$(info_field "$host" "$port" used_memory_human)
    keys=$(key_count "$host" "$port")
    uptime=$(info_field "$host" "$port" uptime_in_seconds)
    clients=$(info_field "$host" "$port" connected_clients)
    limit=$(configured_maxmemory "$host" "$port")
    duration=$(flush_duration_ms "$host" "$port")
    server=$(hostname)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Controlled clearing (eviction) of an in-memory data store instance.
set -uo pipefail

REDIS_CLI=${REDIS_CLI:-redis-cli}

parse_host() {
    local instance=$1
    printf '%s\n' "${instance%%:*}"
}

parse_port() {
    local instance=$1
    case $instance in
        *:*) printf '%s\n' "${instance##*:}" ;;
        *)   printf '%s\n' "6379" ;;
    esac
}

rs() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    shift 2
    "$REDIS_CLI" -h "$host" -p "$port" "$@" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
}

info_field() {
    local host=$1 port=$2 field=$3
    local raw
    raw=`rs "$host" "$port" INFO ALL`
    printf '%s\n' "$raw" | awk -F: -v key="$field" '$1 == key { print $2; exit }'
}

key_count() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    local size
    size=`rs "$host" "$port" DBSIZE`
    printf '%s\n' "${size:-0}"
}

configured_maxmemory() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    local pair
    pair=`rs "$host" "$port" CONFIG GET maxmemory`
    printf '%s\n' "`printf '%s\n' "$pair" | sed -n '2p'`"
}

flush_duration_ms() {
    local host=$1 port=$2
    local start end
    start=`date +%s%3N`
    rs "$host" "$port" FLUSHDB >/dev/null
    end=`date +%s%3N`
    printf '%s\n' "$(( end - start ))"
}

evict() {
    local instance=$1
    local host port
    host=`parse_host "$instance"`
    port=`parse_port "$instance"`

    if [ "`rs "$host" "$port" PING`" != "PONG" ]; then
        printf 'Cannot reach data store instance %s\n' "$instance" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local version memory keys uptime clients limit duration server
    version=`info_field "$host" "$port" redis_version`
    memory=`info_field "$host" "$port" used_memory_human`
    keys=`key_count "$host" "$port"`
    uptime=`info_field "$host" "$port" uptime_in_seconds`
    clients=`info_field "$host" "$port" connected_clients`
    limit=`configured_maxmemory "$host" "$port"`
    duration=`flush_duration_ms "$host" "$port"`
    server=`hostname`

    printf 'Cleared %s keys from data store v%s on %s:%s (host %s) in %s ms; ' \
        "$keys" "$version" "$host" "$port" "$server" "$duration"
    printf 'memory used %s of limit %s bytes, uptime %s s, %s connected clients.\n' \
        "$memory" "$limit" "$uptime" "$clients"
}

main() {
    if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s <host[:port]>\n' "`basename "$0"`" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    evict "$1"
}

main "$@"

Example input is a service manager target. Example output is a summary of the boot performance metrics outputting all requested details.

The script downloads a web page and extracts key structural information for analysis. The `scrape(website)` logic needs to extract the main title text of the page, count the total number of hyperlinks present in the markup, determine the total number of image tags on the page, extract the meta description content string, calculate the total word count of the visible body text, find the primary domain name of the website, determine the total size of the downloaded page in kilobytes, retrieve the hypertext transfer protocol response time in milliseconds, and get the current date and time of the scrape. The script outputs a summary report detailing the page title, hyperlink count, image count, meta description, word count, domain name, page size, response time, and scrape date. Example input is a uniform resource locator string. Example output is a sentence stating a page was scraped bringing all extracted properties together.
